knowledge:
- key_parameters: part.weights=Specifies the weighting of the taxa/parts (e.g., 'enorm.x.gm.counts', 'gm.counts', or 'uniform') ;; ilr.weights=Specifies the weighting of the PhILR space using phylogenetic branch lengths (e.g., 'blw.sqrt') ;; abund_values=Specifies which assay to use when inputting a TreeSummarizedExperiment object (e.g., "counts.shifted") ;; return.votes=Used in name.balance() to return the taxonomic voting details for the numerator and denominator clades (e.g., c('up', 'down'))
- alternatives: TreeSummarizedExperiment (TreeSE) via the mia package and phyloseq containers are supported as alternatives to passing raw matrices and tree objects.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing compositional microbiome survey data with an associated phylogenetic tree, and you want to perform standard multivariate statistical analyses (like ordination, classification, or regression) in a mathematically robust real space.
- pitfalls: Do not normalize counts to relative abundances before calling philr(), as preset part weightings (e.g., enorm.x.gm.counts) rely on raw count magnitudes; closure is applied internally. The phylogenetic tree must be rooted and binary (use ape::multi2di if not binary). The tree must be pruned to match filtered taxa (using ape::keep.tip) to avoid keeping filtered nodes.

workflows.name: philr_transform_and_analysis
workflows.intent: Transform compositional microbiome data using a phylogenetic tree into PhILR balances, perform ordination, identify key balances distinguishing sample groups, and visualize them.
workflows.stages:
1. Filter low-abundance taxa and prune the phylogenetic tree using ape::keep.tip.
2. Add a pseudocount to the count matrix to handle zeros.
3. Check and resolve tree multichotomies, and label internal nodes using makeNodeLabel.
4. Transform the count data into PhILR space using philr.
5. Calculate Euclidean distances and perform MDS ordination.
6. Identify key balances using sparse logistic regression with glmnet.
7. Name the significant balances using name.balance.
8. Map and annotate balances on the phylogenetic tree using name.to.nn, geom_balance, and annotate_balance.
9. Convert PhILR coordinates to long format using convert_to_long for downstream plotting.
workflows.code:
tse <-  GlobalPatterns %>% subsetByPrevalentTaxa(
                               detection = 3,
                               prevalence = 20/100,
                               as_relative = FALSE)
variable.taxa <- apply(assays(tse)$counts, 1, function(x) sd(x)/mean(x) > 3.0)
tse <- tse[variable.taxa,]
tree <- ape::keep.tip(phy = rowTree(tse), tip = rowLinks(tse)$nodeNum)
rowTree(tse) <- tree
assays(tse)$counts.shifted <- assays(tse)$counts + 1 
is.rooted(tree)
is.binary(tree)
tree <- makeNodeLabel(tree, method="number", prefix='n')
rowTree(tse) <- tree
tax <- rowData(tse)[,taxonomyRanks(tse)]
name.balance(tree, tax, 'n1')
otu.table <- t(as(assays(tse)$counts.shifted, "matrix"))
tree <- rowTree(tse)
metadata <- colData(tse)
tax <- rowData(tse)[,taxonomyRanks(tse)]
human.samples <- factor(colData(tse)$SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Mock", "Skin", "Tongue"))
gp.philr <- philr(otu.table, tree, 
                  part.weights='enorm.x.gm.counts', 
                  ilr.weights='blw.sqrt')
gp.philr <- philr(tse, abund_values = "counts.shifted",
                  part.weights='enorm.x.gm.counts', 
                  ilr.weights='blw.sqrt')
pseq <- convertToPhyloseq(tse, assay.type="counts.shifted")
gp.philr <- philr(pseq, 
                  part.weights='enorm.x.gm.counts', 
                  ilr.weights='blw.sqrt')
gp.dist <- dist(gp.philr, method="euclidean") 
d <- as.data.frame(cmdscale(gp.dist))
colnames(d) <- paste0("PC", 1:2)
d$SampleType <- factor(metadata$SampleType)
ggplot(data = d,
  aes(x=PC1, y=PC2, color=SampleType)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Euclidean distances with phILR")
glmmod <- glmnet(gp.philr, human.samples, alpha=1, family="binomial")
top.coords <- as.matrix(coefficients(glmmod, s=0.2526))
top.coords <- rownames(top.coords)[which(top.coords != 0)]
(top.coords <- top.coords[2:length(top.coords)])
tc.names <- sapply(top.coords, function(x) name.balance(tree, tax, x))
votes <- name.balance(tree, tax, 'n730', return.votes = c('up', 'down'))
votes[[c('up.votes', 'Family')]]
votes[[c('down.votes', 'Family')]]
tc.nn <- name.to.nn(tree, top.coords)
tc.colors <- c('#a6cee3', '#1f78b4', '#b2df8a', '#33a02c', '#fb9a99')
p <- ggtree(tree, layout='fan') +
  geom_balance(node=tc.nn[1], fill=tc.colors[1], alpha=0.6) +
  geom_balance(node=tc.nn[2], fill=tc.colors[2], alpha=0.6) +
  geom_balance(node=tc.nn[3], fill=tc.colors[3], alpha=0.6) +
  geom_balance(node=tc.nn[4], fill=tc.colors[4], alpha=0.6) +
  geom_balance(node=tc.nn[5], fill=tc.colors[5], alpha=0.6)
p <- annotate_balance(tree, 'n16', p=p, labels = c('n16+', 'n16-'),
                 offset.text=0.15, bar=FALSE)
annotate_balance(tree, 'n730', p=p, labels = c('n730+', 'n730-'),
                 offset.text=0.15, bar=FALSE)
gp.philr.long <- convert_to_long(gp.philr, human.samples) %>%
  filter(coord %in% top.coords)
ggplot(gp.philr.long, aes(x=labels, y=value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill='lightgrey') +
  facet_grid(.~coord, scales='free_x') +
  labs(x = 'Human', y = 'Balance Value') +
  theme_bw()
gp.philr.long %>%
  dplyr::rename(Human=labels) %>%
  dplyr::filter(coord %in% c('n16', 'n730')) %>%
  tidyr::spread(coord, value) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=n16, y=n730, color=Human)) +
  geom_point(size=4) +
  labs(x = tc.names['n16'], y = tc.names['n730']) +
  theme_bw()
